The electromagnetic field solution for a spherical invisibility cloak with an active device inside is established.
Extraordinary electric and magnetic surface voltages are induced at the inner boundary of the spherical cloak.
The surface voltages prevent electromagnetic waves from going out of the concealed region.
The phase and handness of polarized waves obliquely incident on the inner boundary are kept in the reflected waves.
The surface voltages are found to be exactly equal to the auxiliary scalar potentials at the inner boundary.
The field inside the concealed region exists in the form of standing waves, with zero time-averaged Poynting power.
When the frequency goes to zero, the electric surface voltage V_E becomes zero while the magnetic surface voltage V_H survives for an electric dipole, and vice versa for a magnetic dipole.
The cloak for static magnetic field can be realized artificially using superconductors to create the necessary surface current.
The surface voltages do not violate Maxwell's equations, but are a rare phenomenon in nature.
The paper provides a rigorous mathematical treatment of the electromagnetic field solution inside the concealed region.

The inner radius of the cloak layer is set at R1, and the outer radius is R2.
The background material in the region r < R1 has permittivity ε1 and permeability μ1.
The cloak layer is made of an anisotropic and inhomogeneous medium with specified permittivity and permeability tensors.
The electromagnetic waves are decomposed into TE and TM modes with respect to the radial direction.
